## Today {#today}

| Format | Holds | Session part |
|---|---|---|
| FASTQ / FASTA | sequences | 1 |
| GTF, BED, bedGraph, bigWig | where things are | 2 |
| SAM / BAM | alignments | 3 |

## FASTQ: four lines per read {#fastq}

```
@A00123:456:HXXXXDSX2:1:1101:10004:1000 1:N:0:ACGTACGT+TGCATGCA
TTGCAGGTCTTCAGCAGTTCCTTGAACTCGTCCAGGTTGATCTTGGCCTTCAGGTTGTCG
+
FFFFFFFFFFFF:FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF:FFFFFFFFFF,FFFFFFFFFFFFFF
```

1. `@` name · 2. bases · 3. `+` · 4. one quality character per base

## The header {#fastq-header}

```
@A00123:456:HXXXXDSX2:1:1101:10004:1000 1:N:0:ACGTACGT+TGCATGCA
 instrument:run:flowcell:lane:tile:x:y   read:filtered:control:index
```

- Before the space: the **cluster**, same in R1 and R2
- `1` / `2`: which read
- Public archives rewrite it: `@SRR1039508.1 ...`

## Quality scores {#phred}

$Q = -10 \log_{10} P(\text{error})$

| Q | Wrong 1 in | Char (Phred+33) |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | 10 | `+` |
| 20 | 100 | `5` |
| 30 | 1,000 | `?` |
| 40 | 10,000 | `I` |

NovaSeq bins qualities: mostly `F` (37), some `:` and `,`.

## R1 and R2 are a matched pair {#pairs}

Line *n* of R1 ↔ line *n* of R2. Never filter or sort one alone.

```bash
zcat $DATA/N61311_untrt_R1_001.fastq.gz | head -1
zcat $DATA/N61311_untrt_R2_001.fastq.gz | head -1
```

## FASTA: reference sequences {#fasta}

```
>chr1
NNNNNNNNNN...TAACCCTAACCC...
```

| | Genome FASTA | Transcriptome FASTA |
|---|---|---|
| One entry per | chromosome | transcript (isoform) |
| Introns | yes | no |
| Used by | HISAT2, STAR | Salmon, kallisto |

**Build** (GRCh38 = hg38) and **names** (`chr1` vs `1`) must match everywhere.

::: {.book-link}
[Sequence files](../rna-seq/sequence-files.html)
:::

## Coordinates: 0-based vs 1-based {#coordinates}

```
bases:              A   C   G   T   A   C
1-based (GTF, SAM): 1   2   3   4   5   6
0-based (BED):    0   1   2   3   4   5   6
```

**BED start = GTF start − 1.** End is the same.

## GTF: the gene annotation {#gtf}

```
chr1 HAVANA exon 11426 11671 . + . gene_id "ENSG..."; transcript_id "ENST..."; gene_name "DDX11L2";
```

| Col | | Col | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | chromosome | 6 | score |
| 2 | source | 7 | **strand** |
| 3 | **feature** (gene, transcript, exon) | 8 | frame |
| 4–5 | start–end (1-based) | 9 | attributes |

gene → transcripts → exons. Use **IDs** (ENSG), not names.

## BED: simple intervals {#bed}

```
chr7   5527147   5530601   ACTB    0   -
```

- BED3: chrom, start, end · BED6: + name, score, strand
- **BED12**: + blocks = exons → a whole transcript on one line

```bash
bedtools intersect -a genes.bed -b regions.bed -u
bedtools getfasta -fi genome.fa -bed genes.bed -s
```

## bedGraph and bigWig {#bigwig}

| | bedGraph | **bigWig** |
|---|---|---|
| | BED3 + value | same data |
| Format | text | binary, indexed, zoom levels |
| Use | small regions | **genome browsers**, metagenes |

```bash
bigWigInfo sample.bw
bigWigToBedGraph sample.bw stdout -chrom=chr7 -start=5527000 -end=5531000
```

::: {.book-link}
[Genes and coordinates](../rna-seq/annotation-files.html)
:::

## SAM / BAM {#sam-bam}

| SAM | BAM | CRAM |
|---|---|---|
| text | binary, compressed | smaller, needs the reference |

```bash
samtools view -H sample.bam | head     # header: @SQ chromosomes, @PG history
samtools view sample.bam | head -2     # alignments
```

## The 11 columns {#sam-columns}

```
read1  163  chr7  5527760  60  45M1102N55M  =  5528950  1290  TTGCAGG...  FFFF...  NH:i:1
```

| # | | # | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | read name | 7–8 | mate chrom, position |
| 2 | **FLAG** | 9 | fragment span |
| 3–4 | chrom, position (1-based) | 10–11 | sequence, quality |
| 5 | **MAPQ** | 12+ | tags (`NH`, `NM`, `XS`) |
| 6 | **CIGAR** | | |

## FLAG and CIGAR {#flag-cigar}

**FLAG** = sum of bits: 1 paired · 2 proper pair · 4 unmapped · 16 reverse ·
64 read 1 · 128 read 2 · 256 secondary. `samtools flags 163`.

**CIGAR**: `45M1102N55M` = 45 aligned, **1,102 bp intron**, 55 aligned.
`N` is the fingerprint of RNA-seq.

**MAPQ** (HISAT2): 60 unique · 1 two places · 0 many.

## samtools essentials {#samtools}

```bash
samtools view -c -F 260 x.bam      # primary mapped reads
samtools view x.bam chr7:5500000-5600000 | wc -l   # needs x.bam.bai
samtools flagstat x.bam            # summary
samtools idxstats x.bam            # reads per chromosome
samtools sort -o y.bam x.bam && samtools index y.bam
```

::: {.book-link}
[Alignment files](../rna-seq/alignment-files.html)
:::

## Try it {#try-it}

::: {.try}
```bash
grep -v "^#" $GTF | cut -f3 | sort | uniq -c | sort -k1,1nr      # feature types
awk '$3 == "gene"' $GTF | grep -o 'gene_type "[^"]*"' | sort | uniq -c | sort -k1,1nr | head
samtools flags 99; samtools flags 147
```
:::

Which gene type is most common? Decode FLAGs 99 and 147.

## Recap {#recap}

- FASTQ: 4 lines; Phred+33; R1 ↔ R2
- References must **match** (build, names, release)
- **BED 0-based**, GTF/SAM 1-based
- bigWig for looking; BAM for everything about reads

Next: **cleaning and checking reads**.
